reviews.text: The Three Gorges Museum in Chongqing is definitely one of the must-do itineraries when visiting the city. Located right across from the Great Hall of the People, the museum itself is modern and impressive, both in scale and design. Inside, you’ll find well-curated exhibits that cover a wide range of topics—from the history and culture of Chongqing to the monumental Three Gorges Dam project, ancient artifacts, and even wartime history. The exhibitions are detailed and engaging, offering a good mix of cultural relics, multimedia, and reconstructed scenes that bring history to life. You can easily spend half a day here walking through the different galleries, and there’s a lot to absorb, so pacing yourself is key. It’s not just about the Three Gorges; it’s also a window into the heritage of the entire region. The museum is free to enter, which makes it even more worthwhile. With its thoughtful displays, spacious layout, and comprehensive storytelling, it’s a great place for both history lovers and casual visitors who want to understand Chongqing beyond its food and scenery.

The dome shaped China Three Gorges Museum is free to public, and it displays four main themes for educational, research and preservation purposes. You can learn the ancient Ba-Yu culture and history, early Chongqing and the epic Three Gorges Dam. The museum also has a large collection of relics and artifacts, and all are the original versions. Entrance is free, however you need to pre-register online and generate a QR code for the security guard to scan upon entering. The museum is very popular among domestic tourists too, so be prepared to wait in line for the checking of tickets and also security screening. Suggested time is 1-2 hours depending on how detailed you wanna read the descriptions of the artifacts. Most of it is in Chinese though.
The museum has many floors and a huge number of exhibits. It is a great place to learn about Bayu culture. There are drinking water, toilets and other services.

Museum about the geography, culture and history of the three gorges area of China (Yangtze River Civilisation). Wonderful museum, but there is too much to see! There are too many rooms, by the end we were tired and rushing through the rooms in order to finish our visit sooner. Other than that, it's a great visit with a lot of interesting stuff.

There are several exhibitions showing the history of Chongqing in different time periods. Most of the text descriptions are in Chinese only, so you can use a translator application on your phone. The entrance is free of charge. There are also many different souvenir shops inside
Great place to learn about the history of Chongqing! You need to download app from WeChat. There’s a QR code you need to scan and make a reservation.

First, i would like to give a notice in advance for all traveller and especially solo traveller, this place closed on every monday. From Tuesday to Sunday, they open until 16:30. The place is quite huge, its amazing. The place is near Chongqing people square, there is a big park. You can see Chongqing People Auditorium from across the place. Huge and enourmous architecture. Near the place there a few restaurant such as KFC and Burger King, some gift store also there.

A lot of historical cultural relics. Entrance is free but required to scan a QR code & fill in some basic personal details & a must to input a local mobile number. I didn't have a local number & I approached a helpful staff, he helped punch in some digits & submission was successful. 😆
I love seeing all the ancient artifacts in this museum as I walked out. It looked across the way I thought I was in beijing

Great museum where you can learn a lots about China history not just of the Three Gorges Damn. You should expect to spend at least an hour here. The place is free of charge. I would give a five-star except for that there a lot of exhibitions with only Chinese description so you can't really know what it is.
A large five-story museum showcasing various aspects of Chinese history. Its location is the opposite of Chongqing's Tiantan.

Good exhibits on the local area and the Three Gorges, particularly the Ba people that lived here. The geologic history of the gorges was interesting, and I enjoyed that they had river stones from before the dam was put in. They also had an informative, if a bit random, exhibit on all the different minorities throughout China. The top floor was filled with the collection of a benefactor who collected as many things as he could during the Cultural Revolution, so it's a bit of a mish-mash, but there are beautiful ceramics and calligraphy from the various dynasties. My only complaint is there's no air-conditioning in it, so it can get sweltering.

Free entrance. Great porcelain artifacts and statutes. There is an antique store on the first floor towards the back of the gift shop. It's worth a visit. Some real antiques you can actually touch and buy if you can haggle a fair price.
A section is cool showing artifacts dug out. But nothing on how the Dam was built. No English explanations.
They are closed on Monday. Nice place to visit if bored. Exhibitions are not overwhelming.
Good museum that covers a lot of ground and houses many artifacts. An audio guide is recommended for those who don’t read Chinese.

Beautiful museum showcasing the lives of the people along the 3 gorges and it’s history. Beautiful artifacts and tons of exhibits to explore. Cater at least 2.5hours if you want to explore every exhibit. Don’t miss the amazing 360 panoramic documentary of the before and after construction of the dam and how it affects the look of the Yangtze river.
Pretty nice museum, but it could use better translations for international accessibility.
Very good museum that you can see many China history including yangzhe river three gorges.

Four floors of hot China action. To get to this museum take the green line to Zengjiayan and walk through the long tunnel. You'll get to a square with dance groups, and the museum is right there. The bottom floor has an exhibit about the 3 gorges region of the Yangtze River. The exhibit is not particularly focused and covers everything from wildlife in the area to the types of rock in the gorges. This exhibit was one of the only ones with some English. Other exhibits in the museum include ceramics, calligraphy, minority populations in China, and coins from China's past. Most only in Chinese. Actually the coolest for me was on the top floor. It detailed the life of a Dutch diplomat who studied Chinese in the early 1900s and eventually married a Chongqing lady. He seemed to have lived an interesting life.

Quite crowded, hard to look at things without being disturbed by people looking next to you almost touching, walking around you at all times you have no personal space here. Small bits of information written in English, however there is an audio guide to purchase. Not that informative and didn’t line up with some of the exhibits. Japanese war was interesting.

The Three Gorges Museum is a captivating testament to the rich cultural heritage and natural wonders of the Three Gorges region in China. Situated in Chongqing, this museum offers an immersive journey through the history, art, and geology of the area, showcasing a diverse range of artifacts, exhibits, and interactive displays. From ancient artifacts dating back thousands of years to modern interpretations of the region's landscapes and traditions, visitors are treated to a comprehensive exploration of this iconic landscape. The museum's striking architecture and state-of-the-art facilities enhance the experience, making it a must-visit destination for anyone interested in the cultural and natural treasures of the Three Gorges.
Worth the visit to get an idea of the history of the Chongqing region and country in total. Recommended visit: at least half a day. Quite crowded in the weekdays. English audio guides available

The geologic history of the gorges was interesting, and I enjoyed that they had river stones from before the dam was put in. They also had an informative, if a bit random, exhibit on all the different minorities throughout China. The top floor was filled with the collection of a benefactor who collected as many things as he could during the Cultural Revolution, so it's a bit of a mish-mash, but there are beautiful ceramics and calligraphy from the various dynasties. My only complaint is there's no air-conditioning in it, so it can get sweltering

Interesting place. I expected most of the museum to be focused on the engineering of the project. There's a lot on thst, but I was surprised how much of the museum is dedicated to the human history of the region and the displacement of all the people whose homes and villages were submerged once the dam was complete. Very cool place. Audio guides at the front in a few languages.

A free museum that includes many exhibit halls and interactive exhibits about the gorges and Chinese history around it. Many of the exhibits have no English translations which makes it difficult to follow although translation services are available. I would recommend the museum if you have some extra time to spend. Also right across the street from the 3 Gorges museum is the people Assembly hall that you can visit.

Wonderful museum with much more than the history of the three gorge project. Well curated but given importance of the history and culture more multilingual signs on exhibits and translation of textual material would be welcome. All that said time ran away from us and we left without seeing everything it has to offer

Generally a good museum with information about the geography, the people, the history, and minority cultures of the area with interesting artifacts and life sized displays of scenes. There are also exhibits about more recent historical events in Chongqing (evolution into the city it is today and events during WWII). There are 4 floors of exhibits and if you want to go through every exhibit in detail, it would take maybe 3-4 hours, depending on your pace. Some exhibits have more English than others but generally enough to get the gist. Be warned, there are sprinklings of propaganda here and there.

While the name of the museum suggests that you will learn about the construction of and relevant facts about the Three Gorges Dam, it is actually way more than that. You may get to know the history and culture of Chongqing somewhat, and there are galleries for some other themes that change every now and then. Most galleries are beautifully designed and artifacts are displayed properly with clear illustrations. Yet, quite a number only have Chinese explanation but not English. A further letdown is the gift shops. There are a couple of them scattered on different floors but they don't look that attractive.

If you cannot go to the real Three Gorges Dam, then you can always visit this site. Amazing feat of engineering to see it. Can be reached by chongqing metro but you must walk a further distance to the museum. It's located opposite people's park building. One of the crowded place during weekends and public holidays. Make sure to come earlier to see it in details.

A huge museum with many different sections. The Three Gorges Dam part is available with or without audio-guide. A nice visit to learn about China in the past, present and the future.

This place was actually really amazing. My wife and I stopped in on our last day in the area shortly before it closed, and couldn't believe how much there was to see. We couldn't even finish half of it, but it was one the more memorable parts of my visit to China. Highly recommended.

重慶中國三峽博物館位於重慶市渝中區人民廣場，是國家一級博物館，以保護三峽文物和展示巴渝歷史文化為主，館藏文物豐富（含巴蜀青銅器、漢代藝術品）。其核心展覽《壯麗三峽》重現了三峽原貌，與重慶大禮堂、人民廣場共同構成代表性地標，是了解重慶歷史變遷的必遊之地。

最喜歡大陸各地博物館 內藏品太豐富了 讚 重慶中國三峽博物館是集巴渝文化、三峽文化、抗戰文化、城市文化等為特色的歷史藝術類綜合性博物館，位於重慶市渝中區人民路，與人民大禮堂相對。 該館於2005年6月18日開館，館藏文物豐富，涵蓋三峽文物、巴渝青銅器、漢代文物等多個門類。 展覽內容包括《壯麗三峽》、《遠古巴渝》、《重慶·城市之路》、《抗戰歲月》等，並設有《重慶大轟炸》半景畫演示和《大三峽》環幕電影等。 博物館實行免費開放，需實名制預約，並提供多種形式的導覽服務。 館藏與特色 館藏特色： 以「古人類標本、三峽文物、巴渝青銅器、漢代文物、西南民族文物、大後方抗戰文物、瓷器、書畫、古琴」等為特色藏品系列。 豐富的展覽： 提供常設展覽，如《壯麗三峽》、《遠古巴渝》、《重慶·城市之路》等，還有《重慶大轟炸》半景畫演示、《大三峽》環幕電影、三峽大壩數字沙盤等展示亮點。

De passage à Chongqing, ne manquez pas la visite de ce musée très riche et très bien aménagé. Depuis 2024, la réservation n'est plus obligatoire, l'accès est facilité et vous pouvez même laisser vos effets dans des casiers sécurisés pour profiter pleinement de la visite. Les collections sont remarquables et traitent de l'histoire de cette formidable région.
重慶中國三峽博物館，又名重慶博物館，是與重慶人民大禮堂正對的國家級博物館。 在西南博物院基礎上發展，現擁有館藏文物十多萬件，逐步形成了以古人類標本、三峽文物、巴蜀青銅器、漢代文物、西南民族文物、社建文物、宋元明清書畫、古琴、古墨等為特色的藏品。 是了解四川巴蜀歷史文化的必訪景點。
